newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Q3 current account surplus at US$3.95 bln.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Q3 current account surplus at US$3.95 bln.

text.p: Taiwan's current account posted a surplus of US$3.95 billion in the third quarter compared with a surplus of $552 million a year earlier, the central bank said on Wednesday.

The growing surplus was a direct reflection of Taiwan's rejuvenating exports, with commodity trade showing a quarterly surplus of US$5.881 billion, sharply higher than the US$3.635 billion surplus in the third quarter of 1995, the central bank said in a statement.
Direct investment and other long-term capital registered a net outflow of US$332 million in the third quarter, compared with a net inflow of $310 million a year earlier, it said.
The bank attributed the net outflow of direct investment and other long-term capital to increasing overseas investments by Taiwan people buying foreign stocks.
These outflows outweighed inflows of foreign equity funds into Taiwan's stock exchange.
Short-term capital also registered a net outflow of $1.652 billion in the quarter, compared with a year-earlier net outflow of $8.276 billion.
Foreign assets of the central bank increased $1.556 billion in the third quarter, against a decrease of $6.486 billion in the same period a year earlier.
